name: Republic of the Congo
summary_text: Republic of the Congo is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal (never criminalised); EUAA COI (2024) documents societal discrimination, police harassment, and absence of protection; no LGR; small underground community.

sources.claim_summary: EUAA COI Query Response Q29-2024 (May 2024) on the Republic of the Congo: situation of LGBTIQ people covering legislation and implementation, treatment by the state and society, availability of state protection, and access to support services, for the period January 2022 to May 2024. Same-sex conduct is not criminalised but public-expression provisions are applied; state protection is limited.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This State Department URL is for the DRC 2021 report (fetched under a Republic-of-the-Congo pick); the DRC 2021 report's SOGI section documents societal discrimination and violence.

sources.title: Republic of the Congo - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2022 Human Rights Report for the Republic of the Congo: official assessment including the SOGI section - same-sex conduct not criminalised, but societal discrimination documented; no legal gender recognition.

sources.title: Republic of the Congo - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for the Republic of the Congo: official assessment including the SOGI section - continuing societal discrimination and absence of protections.

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for the Republic of the Congo: documents suspected killings of detainees, mob violence, rape, extortion by armed elements, poor prisons, and societal discrimination - general baseline.
